nodes.content: Develop decentralized multi-agent reinforcement learning that adapts to unfamiliar teammates without destabilizing coordination under partial observability.
requirements: Achieve 20% higher normalized held-out teammate return than matched nonadaptive policies under identical observation constraints.
Retain 95% of familiar-team return without teammate identities, communication, or test-time parameter sharing.

nodes.content: Train decentralized local-history teammate-belief adapters that confidence-gate residual actions atop frozen familiar-team policies using diverse training partners.
Can belief-confidence gating activate residual actions for unfamiliar partners while preserving frozen-policy behavior with familiar partners?
History-gated residuals at unfamiliar-partner probability >0.8 improve held-out normalized return ≥20% over frozen policies while retaining ≥95% familiar return.
Train history-only adapters; sweep confidence thresholds around 0.8 on held-out and familiar partners against frozen baselines under identity-free decentralized inference.
Run 0.6–0.9 gate sweeps on PartnerShift-PO, comparing held-out normalized return and familiar retention against frozen policies across 10 seeds.
On PartnerShift-PO, gating at 0.8 raised held-out normalized return from 0.50 to 0.62, retaining 97% familiar baseline (10 seeds).
Select the 0.8 gate for PartnerShift-PO follow-up because held-out return rose 24% and familiar retention reached 97%.
PartnerShift-PO gate-sweep report contains ten-seed return tables, familiar-retention ratios, frozen-baseline comparisons, and 0.6–0.9 threshold configurations.
Using the selected 0.8 gate and sweep configurations, compare held-out and familiar returns against frozen baselines on disjoint PartnerShift-PO families.
On disjoint PartnerShift-PO switchers, the 0.8 gate achieved 0.56 versus frozen 0.52 held-out return and 93% familiar retention.
Change-point-calibrated belief gating with clipped residuals will improve switcher held-out return ≥20% over frozen baselines while retaining ≥95% familiar return.
Fit local-history change-point calibration, clip residual actions, then test disjoint switchers and familiar teams against frozen baselines.
Fit change-point-calibrated gates with residual norms clipped at 0.2; evaluate disjoint PartnerShift-PO switchers and familiar teams across 10 seeds.
On disjoint PartnerShift-PO switchers, calibrated clipping achieved 0.60 versus frozen 0.52 held-out return (15% gain), despite 96% familiar retention.
Sweep change-point windows (4, 8, 16) and residual clips (0.2, 0.3, 0.4) on disjoint PartnerShift-PO switchers and familiar teams.
On PartnerShift-PO switchers, eight-step calibration and 0.3 residual clipping achieved 0.64 versus frozen 0.52 held-out return and 96% familiar retention.
Eight-step change-point gating with 0.3-clipped residuals yields ≥20% held-out gains and ≥95% familiar retention across switch frequencies.
Stratify PartnerShift-PO by 4–32-step switch intervals; compare the eight-step, 0.3-clipped adapter with frozen policies on held-out and familiar returns.
Evaluate the eight-step, 0.3-clipped adapter against frozen policies at 4-, 8-, 16-, and 32-step PartnerShift-PO switches across 10 seeds.
Across 4–32-step PartnerShift-PO switches, held-out normalized return exceeded frozen baselines by 21–27%; familiar retention was 95–97% (10 seeds).
Ablate change-point calibration and residual clipping across PartnerShift-PO switch intervals, comparing held-out return and familiar retention against frozen policies.
With 4-step episodes withheld from calibration, the eight-step/0.3 adapter gained only 16% held-out return and retained 94% familiar return.
Multi-timescale change-point gating with familiar-policy rollback will deliver ≥20% held-out gain and ≥95% familiar retention on unseen four-step switches.
Train 2/8-step change-point gates without four-step calibration, add uncertainty-triggered rollback, then compare withheld switchers and familiar teams against frozen baselines.
Evaluate 2/8-step gates with uncertainty-triggered rollback on withheld four-step PartnerShift-PO switches and familiar teams versus frozen policies across 10 seeds.
On withheld four-step switches, multi-timescale rollback achieved 0.63 versus frozen 0.52 held-out return (21% gain) and 96% familiar retention.
Ablate two-step gating and uncertainty rollback separately on withheld four-step switchers; measure held-out gain and familiar retention across 10 seeds.
On aliased withheld four-step switchers, full rollback gained 14%; removing rollback gained 22% but retained 92% familiar return.
Local-return-trend rollback replaces uncertainty rollback; 2/8-step gates achieve ≥20% held-out gain on aliased switchers and ≥95% familiar retention.
Tune locally observed reward-trend rollback on training partners; evaluate aliased withheld switchers and familiar teams against frozen policies.
Compare reward-trend versus uncertainty rollback using 2/8-step gates on aliased withheld four-step switchers and familiar teams versus frozen policies.
On aliased four-step switchers, uncertainty rollback gained 21% with 96% familiar retention; reward-trend rollback gained 18%.
Reconcile conflicting 14%/21% uncertainty-rollback gains by retesting reward-trend rollback on matched aliased splits, measuring held-out gain and familiar retention.
On matched aliased splits, reward-trend rollback gained 18% versus uncertainty rollback's 17%; familiar retention was 96%.
Sweep 2/4/8-step reward-trend rollback patience against no-rollback controls on matched aliased splits, measuring held-out gain and familiar retention.
On matched aliased splits, four-step reward-trend patience yielded 21% held-out gain versus frozen policies and 95.5% familiar retention.
Select four-step reward-trend rollback for further evaluation: matched splits met both targets despite earlier reward-trend shortfalls.
Train a trajectory-predictive convention ensemble with decentralized Bayesian policy mixing and a coordination-risk shield, without teammate identities or communication.
Can trajectory-predictive beliefs disambiguate aliased conventions sufficiently for shielded policy mixing to improve held-out return without familiar-team losses?
On aliased PartnerShift-PO switchers, trajectory-predictive shielded mixing yields ≥20% held-out return gain over frozen policies with ≥95% familiar retention.
Train convention predictors on local histories, calibrate risk-shielded policy mixing, and benchmark aliased switchers and familiar teams against frozen policies.
Benchmark trajectory-predictive, risk-shielded Bayesian mixing against frozen policies on aliased PartnerShift-PO switchers and familiar teams across 10 seeds.
On aliased PartnerShift-PO switchers, shielded mixing scored 0.64 versus frozen 0.52 held-out return (23% gain), with 97% familiar retention.
Following the 23% gain, stress-test shielded mixing on unseen near-identical conventions against frozen policies, tracking familiar retention.
On unseen near-identical, aliased PartnerShift-PO switchers, shielded mixing gained only 12% over frozen policies despite 97% familiar retention.
Defer shielded mixing as a general solution; its 23% standard-switcher gain fell to 12% on unseen near-identical conventions.
Near-Identical Convention Stress Report records held-out return, familiar retention, frozen-policy baselines, and trajectory-prediction errors for unseen PartnerShift-PO switchers.
Train low-regret diagnostic actions that reveal teammate conventions, with familiar-policy anchoring and decentralized adaptation from local observation histories.
Can low-regret diagnostic actions distinguish near-identical teammate conventions from local observations without sacrificing familiar-team return?
Train local-history diagnostic probes anchored to the familiar policy; compare convention discrimination and held-out/familiar returns against frozen PartnerShift-PO baselines.
Audit stress-report prediction errors against replayed trajectories; compare selected rollback, shielded mixing, and diagnostic probes on held-out/familiar returns.
On near-identical switchers, diagnostic probes gained 22% over frozen policies versus rollback's 17% and mixing's 12%, retaining 96% familiar return.
After the 22% gain, ablate probes across stress-report prediction-error strata; measure convention accuracy, probe regret, held-out gain, and familiar retention.
In high-aliasing stress-report strata, diagnostic probes incurred 0.08 normalized probe regret, yielding 11% held-out gain and 93% familiar retention.
Gate diagnostic probes by predicted regret ≤0.02; expect ≥20% held-out gain and ≥95% familiar retention in high-aliasing strata.
Calibrate local-history probe-regret estimates, gate probes at 0.02, then test high-aliasing PartnerShift-PO strata against frozen policies.
Using prior 22% probe gain and 0.08 high-aliasing regret, test 0.02-regret-gated probes against ungated/frozen baselines on held-out/familiar returns.
In high-aliasing strata, gated probes gained 21% versus frozen and retained 96% familiar return; delayed-reward familiar subgroup retained only 91%.
Retain rollback; defer mixing and gated-probe rollout despite 21% gain, pending safeguards against 91% delayed-reward familiar retention.
Probe-Regret Audit v1 records high-aliasing gains, calibrated regret thresholds, and delayed-reward familiar retention for gated and ungated probes.
